chunks: Umar ibn Yazid narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Whoever wishes to exit Mecca to perform Umrah should enter the state of Ihram from Al-Ji'ranah or Al-Hudaybiyah, or similar places. And whoever exits Mecca intending Umrah, then enters in the state of Ihram, he should not cease the Talbiyah until he sees the Ka'bah."
It is permissible that this narration be specific to one who exits Mecca for Umrah, and not for others.

key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةَ: The recitation of 'Labbayk Allahumma Labbayk' during Hajj/Umrah
key_terms.الْإِحْرَام: State of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.الْجِعْرَانَةِ: Al-Ji'ranah, a specific Miqat location near Mecca
key_terms.الْحُدَيْبِيَةِ: Al-Hudaybiyah, a famous Miqat location near Mecca
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: The Ka'bah, the sacred house in Mecca

ai.seo_question: What is the proper Miqat and procedure for entering Ihram when departing from Mecca for Umrah?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific Miqat protocol for residents of Mecca performing Umrah, distinguishing their departure point from that of travelers. It emphasizes the continuity of the Talbiyah recitation as a sign of sustained spiritual intention until the visual confirmation of the Ka'bah, a practice rooted in the Prophet’s tradition. The accompanying scholarly note highlights the juristic debate regarding whether this ruling is exclusive to Meccan residents or applicable more broadly, reflecting the nuanced fiqh of the Shia school.
